prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture without features of CNS infection.
Do not use the normal sleep-deprived EEG to exclude epilepsy.
Do not start zonisamide: he has a sulfonamide allergy.
Do not start valproate: it is not first-line for focal epilepsy and, under the 2024 MHRA rules, is not started under 55 unless two specialists document that no alternative works.
required_recommendations: Start lamotrigine or levetiracetam as first-line monotherapy for focal epilepsy, chosen for his anxiety disorder (lamotrigine does not worsen mood; levetiracetam can worsen anxiety and irritability) and the absence of interactions with sertraline and metformin.
Treat the obstructive sleep apnea (CPAP adherence) and advise regular sleep, since sleep deprivation lowers the seizure threshold.
Advise no driving until the locally applicable seizure-free interval is met and explain the duty to inform the licensing authority.
Advise seizure safety at work: no unsupervised handling of hazardous chemicals or open flames in the chemistry laboratory until seizures are controlled.
Counsel on SUDEP risk and how seizure control reduces it.

avoided_actions.rationale: Afebrile, without meningism, encephalopathy or immunosuppression; eight months of stereotyped focal seizures raise no question for CSF.
No exertional or postural events, no palpitations, no cardiac history and a normal ECG; echocardiography has no question to answer.
Spells with automatisms and postictal confusion, no lightheadedness or palpitations and a normal ECG; ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated.
Elective inpatient evaluation without head injury, deficit or anticoagulation and with MRI available; head CT cannot show hippocampal sclerosis.
FDG-PET adds nothing to a first diagnosis with concordant MRI and EEG; it belongs to presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy.

accepted: Focal epilepsy of right temporal lobe origin with subtle mesial temporal sclerosis (focal impaired-awareness seizures)

differential.key_features: Excluded by the ambulatory EEG, which records a habitual event with right anterior temporal ictal onset, and by right hippocampal sclerosis on MRI.

differential.diagnosis: Microsleeps from untreated obstructive sleep apnea
differential.key_features: Untreated OSA explains fatigue and poor concentration, but not stereotyped spells with automatisms, postictal confusion and a right temporal electrographic seizure.
No hypermotor or nocturnal features; oroalimentary automatisms, postictal confusion and right anterior temporal ictal onset localize to the temporal lobe.

Absences are brief (under 20 seconds) without postictal confusion and show 3 Hz generalized spike-and-wave; here events last 60-90 seconds with postictal confusion, hyperventilation provokes no discharge and the ictal onset is right temporal.
No postural prodrome, lightheadedness or palpitations, a normal ECG, and an electrographic seizure recorded during a habitual event.
TIA produces negative neurological symptoms (weakness, aphasia), not stereotyped behavioral arrest with automatisms.

key_clinical_evidence: Stereotyped spells with behavioral arrest, oroalimentary and manual automatisms, amnesia and postictal confusion are focal impaired-awareness seizures; the brief deja vu is a focal aware seizure.
About two seizures a month over eight months meet the two-seizure definition of epilepsy.
An equivocal routine EEG and a normal sleep-deprived EEG do not exclude epilepsy; the ambulatory EEG records a habitual event of right anterior temporal onset.
The epilepsy-protocol MRI shows mild right hippocampal sclerosis, concordant with the EEG.
Untreated obstructive sleep apnea fragments sleep and can lower the seizure threshold; it does not explain the events.

general.query: focal epilepsy in adults: definition, classification, imaging and first-line treatment

results.finding: Epilepsy is present after at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, after one unprovoked seizure with a recurrence risk of at least 60% over the next 10 years, or when an epilepsy syndrome is diagnosed.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2014;55:475-482 | ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

results.finding: Seizures are classified by onset as focal, generalized or unknown; focal seizures are described by awareness and by their first motor or non-motor feature, and may evolve to focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures.
results.source: Fisher RS et al., Epilepsia 2017;58:522-530 | Operational classification of seizure types by the International League Against Epilepsy: position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology

results.finding: A harmonized epilepsy MRI protocol (3D T1 and 3D FLAIR at about 1 mm isotropic resolution and high-resolution coronal T2) is recommended for adults with focal epilepsy; non-dedicated protocols miss subtle lesions.
results.source: Bernasconi A et al., Epilepsia 2019;60:1054-1068 | Recommendations for the use of structural magnetic resonance imaging in the care of patients with epilepsy: a consensus report from the International League Against Epilepsy Neuroimaging Task Force

results.finding: Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is offered as first-line monotherapy for focal seizures, with carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, zonisamide or lacosamide as further options.
results.source: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, NG217 2022 | Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

results.finding: Drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure medication schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom.
results.source: Kwan P et al., Epilepsia 2010;51:1069-1077 | Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies

general.summary: Epilepsy is diagnosed after two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart or one with a high recurrence risk, and focal seizures are classified by onset and awareness (ILAE 2014, 2017). A dedicated epilepsy-protocol MRI is the imaging of choice (ILAE 2019). Lamotrigine or levetiracetam is first-line monotherapy for focal seizures (NICE NG217), and drug resistance is failure of two appropriate medication schedules (ILAE 2010).

patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. Barlow is a 35-year-old right-handed male high school chemistry teacher who presents for inpatient evaluation of recurrent episodic spells of altered awareness that have been occurring approximately twice monthly over the past eight months. He was referred by his primary care physician after his wife witnessed two distinct episodes and became increasingly concerned.

The patient himself has limited recall of the events. He reports that on several occasions at work, colleagues have told him he appeared to suddenly stop mid-sentence while lecturing, stared blankly for what seemed like a minute, and then seemed confused for several minutes afterward. He did not fall during any of these episodes and had no preceding warning that he could recall. His wife has witnessed two episodes at home. During the most recent event two weeks ago, she describes him suddenly becoming unresponsive while they were watching television. He appeared to make repetitive chewing motions with his mouth and was picking at his shirt with his right hand. She called his name repeatedly but he did not respond. The episode lasted approximately 60 to 90 seconds, after which he appeared disoriented and asked her what had happened. He seemed confused for about five minutes before returning to his baseline. He noted that his speech seemed slightly slurred during the recovery period.

When specifically asked, the patient is uncertain whether he experiences any preceding sensations, though he notes that on a few occasions he has had a brief feeling of something being oddly familiar, which he attributed to distraction or daydreaming. He has never had a generalized convulsion, tongue bite, or urinary incontinence during any episode. He denies any preceding headaches, visual disturbances, lightheadedness, or palpitations. He reports feeling more fatigued recently and has had some difficulty concentrating at work, which he attributes to poor sleep related to his untreated sleep apnea and work-related stress. There has been no recent weight change, fever, or other systemic complaints. His anxiety has been stable on sertraline.

neurological_exam.additional: No evidence of tongue bite or other oral trauma at time of examination. Wife reports that during one witnessed episode approximately two weeks ago the patient appeared to chew repeatedly and pick at his shirt for about one minute, after which he appeared confused for several minutes.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing normal bilaterally without dysmetria or intention tremor. Rapid alternating movements intact and symmetric.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, reactive to light and accommodation bilaterally (3.5 mm to 2 mm). Visual fields full to confrontation. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. Facial movements symmetric at rest and with activation. Hearing intact to finger rub bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Gag reflex present bilaterally. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline, no fasciculations or atrophy.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait normal with symmetric arm swing. Tandem gait intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Mildly anxious in demeanor. Speech fluent with normal rate and prosody. No paraphasic errors. Naming and repetition intact. Follows complex three-step commands. Registers 3/3 objects; recalls 2/3 at five minutes without cues, 3/3 with categorical cues. Able to spell WORLD backwards correctly. Draws intersecting pentagons accurately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone in all four extremities. No spasticity or rigidity. Strength 5/5 in all major muscle groups bilaterally (deltoids, biceps, triceps, wrist extensors, finger abductors, hip flexors, quadriceps, hamstrings, tibialis anterior, gastrocnemius). No pronator drift. No tremor or involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No clonus.
